subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw make the running gateway the sole owner of shared state DB write/WAL-maintenance access, and should CLI status/health/stability use RPC-first read-only behavior while that owner is active?
rationale: The source boundary is clear enough to keep the issue open, but the fix changes CLI observability, doctor migration timing, gateway ownership, and recovery behavior for a persisted data-loss class store.

options.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make status/health/stability prefer Gateway RPC and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file inspection while a gateway ownership signal is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: Add an explicit gateway lease so non-gateway processes refuse writer-style shared DB opens before broader CLI behavior is refactored.

options.title: Recovery-first hardening
options.body: Implement malformed DB detection, preservation, and quarantine first while tracking prevention as a separate follow-up.

recommendation.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make status/health/stability prefer Gateway RPC and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file inspection while a gateway ownership signal is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared SQLite state DB introduction is the strongest history signal for the gateway/CLI ownership contract decision.
